one_liner: Obsolete 2024 prototype of a C++26 reflection JSON serializer; about 20x nlohmann/json throughput. Now part of simdjson's builder.
what_it_does: A header-only prototype (about 400 lines in 3 headers) that serializes plain C++ structs to compact JSON with no per-type glue code: no to_json/from_json functions and no NLOHMANN_DEFINE_* macros. simdjson::json_builder::to_json_string(obj) returns a std::string, to_json(obj, str) assigns into an existing string, and fast_to_json_string(string_builder&, obj) appends to a reusable buffer. It only serializes; the README's deserialization demo is simdjson's On-Demand doc.get<T>(). The same feature now ships in simdjson v4.0.0+ (2025-09-11) as simdjson::to_json(obj), to_json(obj, str), or `simdjson::builder::string_builder sb; sb << obj;`.
how_it_is_fast: C++26 static reflection (P2996: nonstatic_data_members_of plus member splicing t.[:dm:]) unrolls each struct at compile time into a straight-line series of buffer appends, with no intermediate DOM. The intermediate DOM is where the nlohmann path spends its time. Each key is quoted and escaped at compile time (a consteval to_quoted_escaped), so at run time it is one memcpy of a constant. Everything goes into one reusable, doubling char buffer (string_builder): numbers through std::to_chars, and strings after a 16-byte SSE2/NEON scan that takes a plain memcpy fast path when nothing needs escaping.
when_to_use: In production, use the successor, not this repo. simdjson v4.0.0+ has simdjson::to_json(obj) and string_builder `sb << obj`. On the latest release (v4.6.11), define SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION=1 or pass CMake -DSIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION=ON, with a P2996 compiler (simdjson's p2996/ docker uses clang-p2996).
On simdjson master (unreleased as of 2026-09-26), reflection is auto-detected. Compiling with GCC 16 and `-std=c++26 -freflection` is enough. CMake gets SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION_MODE=AUTO|ON|OFF.

Throughput-bound output of plain aggregates (ints, floats, bools, std::string, std::vector, nested structs) to compact JSON, such as API responses or logs, where nlohmann's build-a-json-tree-then-dump() path is the bottleneck.
Reproducing or studying Lemire's August 2024 numbers, or learning how a minimal P2996 serializer works. json_builder.h is about 150 lines.
when_not_to_use: Any production build. The author declared the repo obsolete on 2025-10-28. It needs the 2024-era Bloomberg clang-p2996 fork with libc++, and the last code change was in September 2024.

Types beyond arithmetic, strings, indexable containers (size() plus operator[]) and aggregates. json_builder.h has no overloads for std::map, std::optional, enums or smart pointers, and it has no field renaming, skipping or pretty-printing. simdjson's successor has all of these (annotations like rename/skip, enums as strings, optional, fractured-JSON pretty printing).

Data whose strings contain control characters. The escape table emits "\x0000"-style sequences, which are not valid JSON; simdjson's version uses \u0000. NaN and infinity go through std::to_chars and come out as nan/inf, which are also not valid JSON.

Large string fields. string_builder::capacity_check doubles the capacity only once, whatever the size of the pending write. A single string bigger than the space left after one doubling (for example, a ~3 KB string into a fresh 1 KB builder) writes past the heap buffer. simdjson's version grows to max(2*capacity, position+needed).
When you need parsing or a DOM. This is a one-way struct-to-JSON writer, not a replacement for nlohmann::json values.

integration.dependencies: The serializer headers need only the standard library plus <experimental/meta> from the clang-p2996 fork. The repo's CMake also fetches simdjson (builder_development_branch), nlohmann/json 3.10.5, reflect-cpp v0.13.0 (patched) and optionally corrosion/Rust for the benchmarks via CPM.
integration.min_toolchain: Bloomberg clang-p2996 fork (2024 snapshot, no version pinned) with -std=c++26 -freflection -stdlib=libc++. The code uses the pre-final single-caret ^T syntax and std::meta::reflect_value, so expect it not to build on compilers with final P2996 syntax (^^, <meta>). Open issue #45 notes the ^^ change. No released compiler is documented as working.
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE2 escape path), aarch64 (NEON path), scalar fallback elsewhere. Benchmarked on Apple M3 Max and Intel Ice Lake. The README supports Linux/macOS via docker and recommends WSL on Windows.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The free functions keep no global state, and to_json_string makes a local string_builder per call. A string_builder instance is not synchronized.

gotchas: The top-level CMakeLists.txt hardcodes CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++, which overrides CC/CXX. It adds -freflection -stdlib=libc++ -std=c++26 through the INTERFACE target, so every consumer inherits libc++.

Before P1306 expansion statements existed, member iteration used a substitute()/replicator workaround. universal_formatter.h includes a non-existent string_builder.hpp and uses the removed name_of, so it is dead code.

Benchmark asymmetry: the nlohmann baseline builds a nlohmann::json object per record, then calls dump() into a fresh std::string. bench_fast_simpler reuses a warmed string_builder instead. The blog does not say which of the three reflection variants (reused builder, fresh std::string, assign) produced the headline MB/s.
string_builder throws std::runtime_error on capacity overflow and uses new[] (so std::bad_alloc is possible). There is no allocator customization.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Every C++ sibling here (Cista++, struct_pack, YAS, bitsery, FBE, ser20) targets binary formats, and SerialXML emits XML. Pick this family (in practice simdjson's builder) when the output must be JSON text from unannotated structs. ffjson is the Go analogue: it generates code ahead of time instead of using compile-time reflection.
verified_claims_summary: Lemire's 2024-08-13 post serialized a Twitter-derived struct (a field subset of twitter.json) and a synthetic JSON-Generator dataset. On an Apple M3 Max: 1900 vs 100 MB/s (19x) and 1800 vs 50 MB/s (36x). On an unnamed Intel Ice Lake: 1800 vs 110 (16x) and 1400 vs 50 MB/s (28x). The baseline was nlohmann/json 3.10.5 (build a json tree, then dump()). Both sides were built with the Bloomberg clang-p2996 fork, Release (-O3), with libc++. MB/s is output bytes over mean time per call. The claims of 10-20% slower than hand-written code and 2x faster than reflect-cpp come with no published numbers.
status_note: Declared obsolete by its authors: only README edits since September 2024, and the 2025-10-28 notice says the functionality now lives in simdjson. It is Apache-2.0 and small enough to read or vendor for study, but for real use take simdjson >= 4.0.0's builder, which is actively maintained (v4.6.11 released 2026-09-05; builder commits through 2026-09-23).
